items.heading: For Most Private
items.text: For most private-sector software, data, and product-company hiring, a BSc CS graduate with a real project portfolio competes on close to equal footing with a BTech CSE graduate, because hiring at this level weighs demonstrated skill heavily. The real, structural gap appears in two specific places: roles and PSU/government posts that explicitly require an engineering degree by name (which a BSc does not satisfy regardless of quality), and step-linked opportunities, since step eligibility and several of its downstream PSU recruitment routes are built around an engineering degree.

rows: You have a real portfolio of projects and coding practice already, regardless of what your college taught.
You want deeper, structured CS/software training your BSc program did not fully cover, especially from a college where BSc CS leaned more theoretical than applied.
MSc Computer Science or M.Tech (lateral entry where allowed)
You are aiming at research, teaching, or a specialised technical track like AI/ML that rewards a stronger formal research foundation.
A government exam route (banking IT, PSU, SSC technical posts)
You want the stability of a government or PSU role and are prepared for a genuinely competitive, separate exam pipeline.
